environment: This is a deterministic in-memory Node.js model of synchronous steps, microtasks, and timers, not a full browser or multi-worker runtime. Predict before running; we can run it after your answer.

cases.surface: single-threaded handler scheduling a promise microtask and a zero-delay timer around synchronous work
cases.question: Predict every printed line in order. Explain why reqA:microtask runs before reqA:io-callback and why reqB:start appears when it does.

criteria.description: Predicts reqA:start, reqA:sync-cpu-done, reqB:start, reqA:microtask, and reqA:io-callback in order.
Explains that synchronous code runs to completion before queued microtasks drain, and microtasks run before timer callbacks.

wrongModels.claim: A zero-delay timer callback runs immediately at the point where it is scheduled, ahead of following synchronous code.

cases.surface: synchronous CPU work delaying when a subsequent handler can issue its database query
cases.question: Predict every printed line. Explain why B:db-issued cannot occur while A's synchronous work is still running.

criteria.description: Predicts A:enter, A:yield, B:enter, B:db-issued, B:yield, thread:free, and B:db-callback in order.
Explains that B's handler cannot execute or issue its DB operation until the single JS thread finishes A's synchronous work and yields.

wrongModels.claim: B issues its database query concurrently while A is still executing its synchronous loop.

cases.surface: external I/O completing during synchronous work while callback execution waits for yield
cases.question: Predict every printed line. Distinguish external I/O completion from callback execution on the JS thread.

criteria.description: Predicts io:issued, sync:still-running(ioDone=true), sync:yield, io:callback-run, and resp:sent in order.
Explains that external I/O completion can occur while synchronous work runs, but the callback still waits until current synchronous execution yields.

wrongModels.claim: External I/O completion preempts synchronous execution immediately or only starts after synchronous code finishes.
